acceptance_criteria.criterion: Close the verified surviving permissive/scoped policy coexistence on staff_performance_metrics and record the name-based sweep exemption hazard.
evidence: DROPPED: 20260926160000:206-208, three `drop policy if exists`. Proven applied: the harness loads the three policies verbatim from 20250818120000:370-371,404-405,435-436, measures the exposure BEFORE, applies the migration twice, and asserts the final policy set is exactly staff_performance_metrics_scoped_insert,_read,_update plus the retained staff_performance_metrics_write. Idempotent across two applies (policy set byte-identical), and the file's own post-condition DO block RAISEs if any of the three names survives, so a partial drop cannot commit silently. SCOPE — a CORRECTION TO THE CRITERION'S FRAMING, STATED NOT PAPERED OVER: public.staff_performance_metrics HAS NO org_id COLUMN (CREATE TABLE 20250818120000:282-301; the harness asserts this against the extracted DDL). DB-013's has_perm(uid, org_id, ...) shape is therefore not expressible here without adding a column, which is a schema change requiring a generated-type change and a backfill and is not a security fix's vehicle. The three new policies are organization-scoped IN SUBSTANCE and entity-keyed IN MECHANISM: staff_performance_metrics_scoped_read/_insert/_update require (venue_id is not null or event_id is not null) AND has_entity_permission(auth.uid(),'Venue',venue_id,<perm>) OR (event_id is not null AND has_entity_permission(auth.uid(),'Event',event_id,<perm>)), with EDIT_EVENT_LOGISTICS for read and ASSIGN_EVENT_ROLES for insert/update - the same two permissions and the same SECURITY DEFINER helper the table's own intended policies used (20260823210100:87-129). A useful side effect: these predicates contain no subquery against another table, so unlike DB-013's staff_members policies they carry NO authenticated table-grant dependency, only a function-EXECUTE one. Whether the table should gain an org_id, and whether adhoc_venue_id should be an authority arm, are routed to HF-DB-014-EVENT-RESOURCES-AND-CALENDAR-READ-SCOPE rather than decided here. adhoc_venue_id is deliberately NOT an arm because adding it would widen access inside a security fix.

evidence: supabase/tests/db014_staff_performance_metrics_scope.harness.sh, EXECUTED: ALL CHECKS PASSED, 76 PASS / 0 FAIL, exit 0, on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster. It is a behavioural proof with a real negative control: an authenticated account holding NO rbac_user_entity_roles row and NO override reads 4 of 4 performance_rating values across both tenants, reads venue B's exact rating (1.0) by id, INSERTs into venue A and REWRITES venue A's rating BEFORE the migration, and the harness asserts the pre-fix write really landed (ROW_A.performance_rating = 0.0) before restoring the fixture. After the migration the same account reads 0 rows, reads 0 performance_rating values, gets an empty result from a targeted cross-tenant read (not an error), INSERT is rejected with `new row violates row-level security policy for table "staff_performance_metrics"`, UPDATE matches 0 rows, DELETE matches 0 rows, and venue A's rating is unchanged. WITH CHECK is proven independently of USING: a venue A manager who CAN read the row is rejected re-scoping it onto venue B and separately rejected stripping its tenant entirely. Every assertion about the chain's own authority helper is made against a precondition that is itself asserted first - ten has_entity_permission preconditions are checked before any denial, so no denial can be vacuously true. The zero-drift catalog postflight supabase/tests/db014_staff_performance_metrics_scope_contract.sql (9 checks, violation rows only, one summary row) is proven able to fail THREE times: removing a scoped policy; re-introducing read_all_metrics WHILE the scoped policy is present (the CP-104 case a scoped-successor check scores as safe); and stripping the tenant-key conjunct, leaving a policy that only fails closed because of has_entity_permission's NULL arithmetic.

DEMONSTRATION THAT IT ACTUALLY FIRES, executed: supabase/tests/db014_sweep_exemption_hazard.harness.sh - ALL CHECKS PASSED, 18 PASS / 0 FAIL, exit 0. It extracts the chain's OWN sweep block (20260823210000:243-314) and runs it against a real catalog holding two policies that differ ONLY by name, both `USING (true)`: the sweep DROPS job_applications_read and KEEPS job_applications_employer_manage_hiring. The detector then reports the survivor as exempt-hiding-permissive; when the same name is re-created with a genuinely scoped body the detector returns zero violations and summary t, and it stays clean after four more policies are added - so it is not a name blacklist. STATED LIMIT: it proves a policy is not merely an authentication test; it cannot prove a policy is correctly scoped. scope_expansions.reason: Acceptance criterion 3 requires a detection check, and the task named scripts/ci/ as the convention. Two files rather than one because the check has two halves that cannot be one file: the static half must not connect to a database (so it can run in any pipeline with no credentials) and the target half must be read-only SQL an operator can run against staging and production. A single file would have had to either connect from CI or re-implement pg_policies parsing in JS, and both were worse. The .test.mjs sibling is the convention for every other scripts/ci check in this repository, run with `node --test` because the vitest include globs do not cover that directory.

A fixture inside the .mjs cannot answer the objection that the rule has never touched a real pg_policies. This harness extracts the chain's OWN sweep block and runs it against a real catalog with two policies differing only by name, which is the only way to show the hazard is real rather than asserted, and it is also what proves the detector fires on a policy the chain itself declined to remove.

READ-ONLY reuse, not edited. The harnesses extract the chain's own CREATE TABLE, guarded policy blocks, rbac table DDL and has_entity_permission text BY LINE RANGE at run time, so the emulated authority cannot drift from the chain. 20250823210000 was read for the sweep block the exemption-hazard harness executes; 20260823221000 and 20260717194541 were read only for the Task 3 disposition and are NOT modified. 20260903120000, 20260911013017, 20260416000323 and 20260821031214 were read only to re-verify the cleared list.
